issue_context.title: Abort the transaction when the placement rules are changed
issue_context.body:
## Development Task

When a local transaction accesses a partition, it will check the placement rules of this partition. In this process, it assumes that the placement rules of these partitions don't change through the transaction. If the placement rules are changed, the assumption is broken, so we must abort the transaction.

## Implementation

Before introducing the solution, I need to introduce how DDL and transactions work currently.

Transactions assume that the table definitions don't change through the whole transaction. When the transaction commits, it will check whether the table definitions are changed. If they are changed, the transaction may do one of these things:
- amend the data it writes, which can avoid abortion.
- abort the transaction. This is not retriable.

Also, TiDB should guarantee that all TiDB instances always read the same schema at the same time. Once the schema changes, the new schema should take effect on all TiDB instances at the same time. This is done by [online DDL schema change](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/docs/design/2018-10-08-online-DDL.md).

Now, we have some things to focus:
- How to collect the table/partition ids which the transaction modifies
- How to check whether the definitions of these tables/partitions are changed through one transaction
- How to collect the relevant table/partition ids when executing a DDL

### How to collect the table/partition ids which the transaction modifies?
This is done by the Table API. All table modification goes to Table API(`table/table.go`), e.g. `AddRecord` is inserting a record, `UpdateRecord` is updating a record. All these APIs collects the table ids into `TransactionContext.TableDeltaMap` by `UpdateDeltaForTable`. So when the transaction commits, it knows which tables are touched.

### How to check whether the definitions of these tables/partitions are changed through one transaction?
Now that we have the table/partition ids, we need to check whether the definitions of them are changed. This is done by the schema version mechanism. Schema version is a global id which indicates the version of the database schema. Everytime a DDL executes, the schema version increases.  
In `SchemaChecker.CheckBySchemaVer`, it gets all schema changes through the transaction by comparing schema versions. `schemaValidator` saves a history of all schema changes(`deltaSchemaInfos`), each of which saves the tables/partitions that are changed. In this way, we can know the definitions of which tables are changed through the transaction.

### How to collect the relevant table/partition ids when executing a DDL?
Here we focus on how to construct `deltaSchemaInfo` when executing a DDL. Everytime PD receives a schema version change, it notifies all TiDB instances to load the schema diffs. TiDB loads schema diffs from TiKV (in `domain.tryLoadSchemaDiffs`), applies them to the in-memory schema, and constructs `RelatedSchemaChange`. `RelatedSchemaChange` will finally be transformed into `deltaSchemaInfos`.

### What need we do to support local transactions?
Almost the whole architecture is already built, so we need to make sure some things are right:
- When altering placement rules, the relevant partition ids are also written into `RelatedSchemaChange` (in `ApplyDiff`)
- The schema version changes when altering placement rules (should already be done)
